title: De lineis curvis non in eodem plano sitis, quae maximi minimive proprietate sunt praeditae

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the geometric set-up and states the problem. Section 3 (end): a space curve is described by two equations, y = y(x) and z = z(x). The first gives the projection onto the plane AOB (the xy-plane). The second gives the projection onto AOC (the xz-plane). Eliminating x gives a relation between y and z, which is the projection onto BOC (the yz-plane). Two projections therefore fix the curve, and the third follows from them.

Section 4 states the variational problem. Find a space curve (y(x), z(x)) that makes the functional J = ∫ V dx a maximum or minimum. V may depend on x, y, z and on derivatives of y and z of any order. V may even contain further integral expressions (isoperimetric or nonlocal terms). The answer needs two equations, one for y in terms of x and one for z in terms of x, which give the two projections.

Section 5 introduces the notation used in the author's earlier work on the two-variable case (the Methodus inveniendi, 1744): dy = p dx, dp = q dx, dq = r dx, and so on, with primed letters for z: dz = p' dx, dp' = q' dx, dq' = r' dx, and so on. Integral terms inside V are set aside for now. V is then treated as an ordinary function V(x, y, z, p, p', q, q', r, r', ...).

The following page writes dV = M dx + N dy + P dp + ... + N' dz + P' dp' + .... It then derives the pair of Euler–Lagrange equations N − dP/dx + d²Q/dx² − ... = 0 and N' − dP'/dx + ... = 0. It does so by freezing one projection at a time.

In modern terms, the page sets up a variational problem for a vector-valued function (y, z) of one independent variable with higher-order Lagrangian. The goal is the system of Euler–Lagrange (Euler–Poisson) equations.
errors: Minor gap: the claim that the two projections onto AOB and AOC always determine the curve assumes the curve can be written as a graph over the x-axis. Curves with segments in planes x = const are excluded. This restriction is implicit in the whole method and is not an error within Euler's framework.

ideas.what: A space curve represented by two projection equations y(x), z(x); the third projection follows by eliminating x
ideas.modern_name: Graph parametrization of a space curve / Monge-style projections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Clairaut (Recherches sur les courbes à double courbure, 1731); Euler
ideas.where_published: Introductio in analysin infinitorum vol. II, appendix (1748)

ideas.what: Extremizing ∫ V dx where V depends on two unknown functions and their derivatives of all orders, possibly with embedded integral formulas
ideas.modern_name: Multi-function higher-order variational problem (system of Euler–Lagrange/Euler–Poisson equations)
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (1744) for the one-function case; Lagrange, Misc. Taurinensia 1760–61 for several functions

ideas.what: Notation dy = p dx, dp = q dx, ... and primed letters p', q', r' for z

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely expository setup: projections of space curves and notation for a two-function variational problem. All of it is standard and already covered in Euler's and Lagrange's published work.
transcription_corrections: The transcription of this page matches the image; no substantive corrections. (On the previous page, 'Quodsi jam z fuerit punctum' should read 'Z' as the point label, and 'axos' is likely 'axes'.)
